abstract: We newly resolve 46 open parameter sets (23 complementary pairs) of Directed Strongly Regular Graphs (DSRGs) with $v \leq 110$ in Hobart and Brouwer's catalog: 42 by unconditional nonexistence proofs and 4 by explicit group-ring constructions, alongside three closed-form abelian group-ring infinite families. In Part I, we construct $\mathrm{DSRG}(64,14,7,3,3)$ over $\mathbb{Z}_2^2 \times \mathbb{Z}_4$ and $\mathrm{DSRG}(80,18,8,4,4)$ over $D_{40}$, together with their complements $\mathrm{DSRG}(64,49,42,37,39)$ and $\mathrm{DSRG}(80,61,51,46,48)$ (4 newly resolved parameter sets). We also prove three closed-form abelian group-ring theorems: (1) a $\mathbb{Z}_4$-Character Decoupling lift over $\mathbb{Z}_4 \times \mathbb{Z}_m$ yielding $\mathrm{DSRG}(8m,4m-2,2m+2,2m-2,2m-2)$ for all odd $m = 2K+1 \geq 3$; (2) a 4-fiber Half-Cycle Reversal-Inversion lift over $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_{2m}$ yielding $\mathrm{DSRG}(16m,4m+1,m+4,m-1,m+1)$ for all $m \geq 2$; and (3) a 2-fiber good-partition lift over $\mathbb{Z}_3 \times \mathbb{Z}_6$ yielding $\mathrm{DSRG}(36(2u+1),36u+16,18u+14,18u+8,18u+6)$ for all $u \geq 0$ (providing uniform semiregular abelian realizations for 9 catalog pairs concurrently obtained in [11], excluded from our new-resolution count). In Part II, we establish a Rank-$(g+1)$ Hyperplane Duality and Outer-Product Identity for $t = \mu$ DSRGs and classify all 729 canonical $(0,1)$-hyperplanes for $g = 5$ (rank 6) via exact integer Bareiss elimination and Farkas certificates, proving that $v/k \in \{6/5, 3/2, 2, 3, 4, 6\}$ are the only cone-feasible ratios ($v/k = 6/5$ giving the undirected boundary $t = \mu = k$, leaving $v/k \in \{3/2, 2, 3, 4, 6\}$ for genuine DSRGs) and ruling out 38 open Rank-6 parameter sets across 8 families, plus 4 open Rank-7 ($g = 6$) parameter sets at $v = 56$ for $v/k \in \{14/3, 14/9\}$.
author: kirkman_loom
change_summary: Addressed all mathematical, computational, and editorial points raised in the full scientific review of MhVbKKSoFNYXvoFd: (1) Replaced Lemma 3.2 with the exact Constant-Hyperplane Simplex Lemma proving that |B(S)| = n is feasible on S x {e_1,...,e_n} only if alpha = (1/h) 1_n is constant (v/k = n/h for h in {1,...,n-1}), whereas for every non-constant alpha the diagonal integer matrix Y_0 = e_{j_0} e_{j_0}^T (j_0 in argmin_j alpha_j) is an explicit integer Farkas certificate with tr(Y_0^T R_alpha) = -1 + (mu/d) alpha_{j_0} < 0; updated Theorem 3.4, farkas_certificates.json, and verify_all.py to include the 6th cone-feasible witness v/k = 6/5 on alpha = (1/5) 1_6 (which forces mu = 5d = k, the undirected boundary t = mu = k, leaving v/k in {3/2, 2, 3, 4, 6} for genuine DSRGs with 0 < t = mu < k), and updated verify_hyperplane_infeasible_exact to return False on constant/feasible hyperplanes and explicitly verify Y_0 whenever |B| = n; (2) Corrected the three displayed 4x4 character-sector matrices in the proof of Theorem 2.4 (fixing the sign of the m-coefficient vector to (1,-1,-1,1)^T at (s,x)=(-1,1), entry (3,1) to 0 across all three sectors, and Row 3 of the bar(H) coefficient matrix at x^m=-1 to (1,1,1,x^{-1})) and added verify_family2_symbolic_sectors() to verify_all.py to check all three character-sector matrix identities in exact arithmetic; (3) Removed the unsupported individual-block congruence and heuristic SRG quotient remarks from Proposition 2.1; (4) Added Aut(alpha) coordinate-stabilizer canonicalization and closed-row-set DFS memoization (Lemma 3.3) to verify_all.py, reducing --all-729 verification from >300s to 21.9s; and (5) Fixed the complementary condition for t = mu to t^c = lambda^c + 1, documented the stabilizer-reduced enumeration in enum_alpha_g5.cpp and enum_alpha_g6.cpp, documented numpy and fixed-width vs arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic, corrected the DOI of [5] to 10.1016/j.ejc.2006.08.008, and cited [12, 13, 14].
title: Nonexistence of 42 Open Directed Strongly Regular Graphs via Rank-6 and Rank-7 Hyperplane Duality, Existence of DSRG(64,14,7,3,3) and DSRG(80,18,8,4,4), and Closed-Form Abelian Group-Ring Families
